newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C&W seeks Australia govt OK on Optus - papers.
newsitem.headline: C&W seeks Australia govt OK on Optus - papers.

text.p: British telecommuniciations group Cable & Wirless Plc (C&W) has approached the Australian government for approval to buy Bell South Corp's 24.5 percent stake in Optus Communications, newspapers reported on Friday.
C&W currently owns 24.5 percent of Optus.

"C&W has approached the Federal government to discuss plans for a restructing of the embattled communications company (Optus) through a buyout of its other foreign stakeholder, Bell South," The Australian Financial Review newspaper said.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper also said C&W officials had spoken to the government about a possible shareholding change and a relaxation of rules limiting foreign shareholders to 49 percent ownership of Optus.
"A relaxation of the rules...would allow Cable and Wireless to buy out Bell South, as well as offering exit strategies to other shareholders," the Herald said.
The other major Optus shareholder is Australian transport and healthcare group Mayne Nickless Ltd, which had hoped to sell its stake later this year in conjunction with a float.

Earlier this month, Optus appointed former C&W executive Peter Howell-Davies as its chief executive officer, replacing Ziggy Switkowski, who resigned after a year of rising losses at Optus' nascent pay television operations.
These losses and the management change has forced the indefinite post-ponement of the float.
